item.title: Edit for SCP-5232
item.description: I was given a lot of feedback on SCP-5232 so I have made an improved version, any feedback on this is much appreciated
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

nt:image-block
| name=SCP-5232
| caption=Image of SCP taken by CLASS-D before they had their eyes set on fire
]]

Item #: SCP-5232

Object Class: Safe

Threat Level: Blue

Special Containment Procedures: [All information regarding SCP-5170 is to be hidden from level 1 personnel or less if a person of such level accesses information regarding SCP-5170 they are to immediately receive Class-B Amnestics. SCP-5232 is to be kept in a 30m2 cell and protocol 202-5232-A

Protocol 202-5232-A forbids any foundation personnel to enter the cell unless they have already come within 30m of this SCP before the protocol was in place, tests with D-CLASS on SCP-5232 is still allowed as long as as the test is done by a level 3 or higher researcher.

Any cleaning of SCP-5232's cell is to be done by a D-CLASS janitor or any janitor who has come in contact with SCP-5232 beforehand and survived.

It has also been concluded impossible to destroy SCP-5232 and impossible to stop it rolling.

Description: [SCP-5232 is a six-sided silver dice of unknown origin. SCP-5232 does not show any anomalies properties until an entity (human, animal, plant and SCP all included) comes within 30m2 of the SCP, if an entity comes within 30m2 the dice will then proceed to roll itself, which tests have shown is completely randomized.

Once it has done this, if the higher value the number value displayed on the top of the dice, the higher level of damage the entity suffers. Tests show there is no way to cancel the anomalous effects and tests show the type of damage/death the entity suffers is also randomized. Also, a roll of one so far appears to guarantee no damage and a roll of six so far appears to guarantee instant death.]

« | SCP-5170 | »

CLASS-D: [D-4546B]

Researcher: [Nadiva Raghe]

Foreword: [Tesing if using a metallic clamp to stop the dice rolling will prove successful]

<Begin Log, [11:53]>

Researcher: [D-4546B please enter the cell and proceed to clamp the dice with the equipment you were given]

CLASS-D: [O K…what should I observe for?]

Researcher: [Anything out of the ordinary, NO more questions!]

Researcher: [Interesting. The dice appears to be melting the clamps and continue to roll itself]

CLASS-D: [I…Is that bad? It looks like its stopped.]

Researcher: [D-4546B I cannot see the number on the top of the dice, what does it show?]

CLASS-D: [It shows a six, why?]

Researcher: [Hmmm, ok I have an idea. D-4546B please proceed to leave the room. You have finished the test]

CLASS-D: [Oh…thank you Dr I hope I did we-]

CLASS-D: [AHHHHHHHHHhhh…]

Researcher: [Ok so it appears by leaves the area death still happens. D-4546B: Cause of Death: A currently unknown type of acid]

Researcher 2: [So Dr Nadiva how did the test go and what did we find out?]

Researcher: [Nothing especially interesting, the dice melted the clamp and then proceeded to still roll.]

Researcher 2: [Ok I shall bring in another D-CLASS, this time I want to see if the subject can be hidden from view and the dice will still roll.]

Researcher 2: [Very well, starting a new log]

<End Log, [12:07]>

Closing Statement: [The dice appeared to melt the clamp meaning test failed and leaving the area to stop the anomalous effects was unsuccessful]

CLASS-D: [D-4546E]

Researcher: [Dr Nadiva Raghe]

Foreword: [Testing if a physical barrier that blocks line of sight between entity and subject will stop the anomalous effects]

<Begin Log, [12:15]>

Interviewer: [D-4546E please proceed into the cell and make sure to keep that riot shield in front of you at all times.]

CLASS-D: [Yes Dr, now what exactly does this SCP do?]

Researcher: [Thats not for you to know, now enter the cell as instructed.]

CLASS-D: [So am I supposed to be looking for something happening? Or some changes in the room?]

Researcher: [D-4546E please position your body camera so I can observe the SCP.]

CLASS-D: [As you wish.]

CLASS-D: [It appears to be rolling itself, is this normal behaviour?]

Researcher: [Yes, now no more questions!]

CLASS-D: [Okay…]

Researcher: [D-4546E please can you tell me what number appears on the top of the dice?]

CLASS-D: [A five, is that nor-]

CLASS-D [Sorry, no more questions]

Researcher: [Nothing appears to be happening around you?]

CLASS-D: [No, but I am starting to feel a little strange.]

Researcher: [I'll get security to escort you to a medical room where we can issue a full-body scan]

CLASS-D: [AHHHh! Whats happened to me?!? I think my bones have melted!]

Researcher: [Please D-4546E remain calm. I'm calling a medical team to come and collect you for now please remain calm.]

CLASS-D [HOW CAN I REMAIN CALM WHEN MY BONES ARE LIQUID!?! AHHHH!]

Research: [Security I need D-4546E tranquillized immediately, thank you.]

Security: [Yes Dr Nadiva.]

Researcher: [Thank you, now please bring D-4546E to a medical bay to receive a full-body scan. D-4546E: Casualties: Liquidized bones]

<End Log, [12:21]>

Closing Statement: [Test unsuccessful however we now think that the higher the roll of the dice the more dangerous effects take place on the subject. However, more tests are required to prove that theory. It must also be noted that the security guard who tranquillized D-4546E had previously come in contact with SCP-5232 and had survived with only a broken leg as a casualty]

CLASS-D group: [D-4546F, D-4546G, D-4546H, D-4546I and D-4546K]

Researcher: [Dr Nadiva Raghe]

Foreword: [Testing if having multiple subjects in the cell affects how the anomaly works]

<Begin Log, [12:32]>

Researcher: [CLASS-Ds please enter the cell together at roughly the same time]

CLASS-D group: [Ok Dr Nadiva]

Researcher: [Thank you now D-4546H, please can you position your body camera so I can observe the SCP.]

D-4546H: [Yes Dr.]

Researcher: [Which one of you entered the cell first?]

D-4546I: [That would be me Dr, why do you ask?]

Researcher: [Please do not ask questions D-4546I, is that clear?]

D-4546I: [Yes, sorry Dr.]

D-4546F: [Dr the dice have stopped moving.]

Researcher: [Yes I can see that thank you. Its value is two, D-4546I do you feel anything strange or are you experiencing any pain?]

D-4546I: [Nothing that I've noticed so far. Oh wait, I appear to somehow have a scratch mark on my left shoulder. However, it's hardly bleeding]

Researcher: [Ok thank you D-4546I. D-4546H: Casualties: Scratch mark of unidentified species on the left shoulder, no serious damage.]

D-4546H: [Dr the dice is rolling again. Im positioning the camera now so you can observe it.]

Researcher: [I can not see the value still, please can you tell me what it shows]

D-4546I: [It shows a four Dr.]

Researcher: [Now D-4546H you were second to enter the cell?]

D-4546H: [Yes correct Dr.]

Researcher: [Please hand the camera over to D-4546G.]

D-4546H: [O…Ok, why what's going to happen to me?]

Researcher: [Please remain clam D-4546H I do not know what will happen, that is why you are here.]

CLASS-D: [Ok? Am I at least make it out alive.]

Researcher: [Most likely, yes. No more questions.]

D-4546H: [Im starting to feel hot, like burning hot. Oww I think I'm starting to burn!]

Researcher: [Please stay calm D-4546H and if you can not then please do not scream.]

D-4546H: [I can tr-]

Researcher: [It appears from the camera that D-4546H has passed out from the pain, is that correct? D-4546H: Casualties: Set on fire for 35 seconds and suffered 3rd-degree burns around the skull.]

D-4546G: [Seems that way Dr.]

Researcher: [Security please can you come in and escort D-4546H to a medical team and D-4546I to receive Class-B Amnestics, thank you]

Security: [Yes Dr Nadiva.]

Researcher: [The two of you that entered last please leave the cell and wait outside the door.]

D-4546G: [That would be me and D-4546F Dr. Should I leave the camera with D-4546K?]

Researcher: [Yes.]

D-4546K: [Okay, so I just wait to see what my fate is yes? And may I ask why they left the room?]

Researcher: [Did you not hear what I said to D-4546I?]

D-4546K: [Right yes, sorry.]

D-4546K: [Its rolled a 2, same as D-4546I]

Researcher: [Interesting, D-4546K please check your left shoulder for a scratch mark.]

D-4546K: [No scratch mark Dr, however, I think my ankle is sprained]

Researcher: [Ok so it seems even though the dice can roll the same value the effect is different. D-4546K: Casualties: Sprained ankle.]

D-4546K: [Dr the dice is rolling again although I am the only one in the room.]

Researcher: [Please can you get D-4546G and D-4546F back in the cell.]

D-4546K: [Yes. You too, Dr Nadiva wants you both back in here!]

Researcher: [The dice has stopped on a one, which one of you entered after D-4546K?]

D-4546G: [That would be me Dr I don't feel any pain or unease.]

Researcher: [Nothing at all?]

D-4546G: [Nothing Dr.]

Researcher: [Ok thank you D-4546K and D-4546G please leave the cell and Security will escort you to receive Amnestics.]

D-4546G: [Ok Dr thank you.]

D-4546F: [That leaves me now Dr? The dice has started rolling again. It's stopped on a six.]

Researcher: [Security please tranquillize D-4546F.]

D-4546F: [WHAT, why?!? What's going to hap-]

Security: [Done.]

Researcher: [D-4546F: Cause of Death: Several lead bullet shots to the cerebral cortex from. It is unknown where these bullets came from as there are no bullet holes in the wall of the cell.

<End Log, [13:01]>

Closing Statement: [Having several subjects in the cell did not affect how the anomalous effects functioned. We now know that the dice will roll one by one starting with who entered first]


No full drafts on the forums.
